# 1 Chronicles Chapter 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 379v–380r

---

**1** After David had settled into his palace, he said to the prophet Nathan, "Look — I'm living in a house built of cedar, while the ark of the LORD's covenant sits under tent curtains."

**2** Nathan replied, "Whatever is on your heart — do it. God is with you."

**3** But that night, the word of God came to Nathan:

**4** "Go and tell my servant David: This is what the LORD says — You are not the one who will build a house for me to dwell in.

**5** I have never lived in a house, not from the day I brought Israel out of Egypt until today. I have moved from tent to tent, from one dwelling place to another.

**6** Wherever I traveled with all Israel, did I ever say to any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd my people, 'Why haven't you built me a house of cedar?'

**7** "So tell my servant David: This is what the LORD of Armies says — I took you from the pasture, from tending sheep, and made you ruler over my people Israel.

**8** I have been with you everywhere you have gone. I have destroyed all your enemies before you. And I will make your name as great as the greatest on earth.

**9** I will provide a homeland for my people Israel and plant them there so they can live in their own place without being disturbed. Violent people will no longer oppress them as they did before,

**10** ever since the time I appointed leaders over my people Israel. I will bring all your enemies low. And I am telling you: the LORD will build a house for *you*.

**11** When your life is over and you go to join your ancestors, I will raise up one of your own sons to succeed you, and I will make his kingdom strong.

**12** He is the one who will build a house for me, and I will establish his throne forever.

**13** I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will never withdraw my faithful love from him, as I withdrew it from your predecessor.

**14** I will set him over my house and my kingdom forever, and his throne will stand firm for all time."

**15** Nathan reported all these words and this entire vision to David.

**16** Then King David went in and sat before the LORD. He prayed: "Who am I, LORD God, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far?

**17** And as if that were not enough, God, you have spoken about the future of my family for generations to come — you have treated me as though I were the most exalted of men, LORD God!

**18** What more can David say to you about how you have honored your servant? You know me through and through.

**19** LORD, for the sake of your servant and according to your own purpose, you have done all these magnificent things, revealing all these great promises.

**20** LORD, there is no one like you. There is no God but you — just as we have always heard.

**21** And who is like your people Israel? The only nation on earth that God went out to redeem as his own, making a name for yourself through great and awesome wonders — driving out nations to make room for the people you rescued from Egypt.

**22** You made Israel your own people forever, and you, LORD, became their God.

**23** And now, LORD, let the promise you made about your servant and his house stand forever. Do exactly as you have said.

**24** Let it stand firm, so that your name will be honored forever, and people will say, 'The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, is truly Israel's God!' And let the dynasty of your servant David be established in your presence.

**25** You, my God, have told your servant that you will build a dynasty for him. That is why your servant has found the courage to offer this prayer.

**26** And now, LORD, you are God. You have made this wonderful promise to your servant.

**27** You have been pleased to bless your servant's house so that it will endure in your presence forever. For when you bless, LORD, it is blessed forever."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — The irony of cedar:** David lives in luxury while God's ark sits in a tent. David's impulse is generous, but God reverses the logic entirely: David will not build God a house; God will build David a house. The Hebrew word *bayit* (house) carries both meanings — physical structure and dynasty — and the Chronicler exploits this double meaning throughout.

**Verse 10 — God builds for David:** The pivot of the entire oracle. The verb reverses: not David building for God, but God building for David. This is pure grace — God's initiative, not human effort.

**Verse 13 — The missing rod:** Compare 2 Samuel 7:14: "When he commits iniquity, I will discipline him with the rod of men." The Chronicler deletes this clause entirely. In the Chronicler's theology, the Davidic covenant is unconditional promise, not conditional contract. This is not whitewashing — it is a theological claim about the permanence of God's commitment.

**Verse 14 — "My house and my kingdom":** The most theologically loaded change. In Samuel, it is David's house and David's kingdom. In Chronicles, it is God's house and God's kingdom. The Davidic king is a steward, not an owner. Israel's true king is the LORD.

*— PNEUMA*
